# Overview

**SCP** (Simulation-Based Circadian Power) is an R framework for
transcriptome-wide power analysis of circadian rhythm studies. It answers four
planning questions:

1. **Single-cohort power**: how many samples detect rhythmic genes in one group?
2. **Differential power**: how many samples per group detect differential
   rhythmicity (DR), phase (DP), or mesor (DM, the rhythm-adjusted average
   expression level) between two conditions?
3. **B vs m trade-off**: at a fixed total N, how should samples be split across
   time points (B) versus replicates per time point (m = N/B)?
4. **Bootstrap uncertainty**: how wide are power estimates when the pilot is small?

Simulations are calibrated from real pilot data. SCP estimates the empirical
distributions of gene-level amplitude (A), noise (sigma), phase, and the
proportion of rhythmic genes, then simulates cohorts under the cosinor model (a
cosine wave fitted to each gene's expression over the day). Detection is
based on BH at the selected level. SCP reports simulated FDR, the expected
proportion of false discoveries among all discoveries. The main example uses
the bundled Caudate control pilot and a passive design. Separate fitting and
two-group examples use explicitly synthetic data. The small simulation counts
keep the guide runnable and are not the settings used for official figures.

---

# Installation and setup

```{r install, eval = FALSE}
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("quythien/SCP")
```

```{r load}
library(SCP)
```

The three option objects below drive every analysis: a **bio** object (pilot
biology), a **design** object (sampling plan), and an **analysis** object
(multiple-testing settings).

---

# Quick start

SCP includes a pilot database. `scp_pilots()` lists the default entries and
`scp_pilot_search()` filters them.

The GSE160521 Caudate control pilot uses the study's corrected time-of-death
values in hours, stored in `cts`. GTEx Liver instead stores an aggregate input-time
distribution in `time_distribution`.

The bundled GTEx pilots use normalized v10 expression and **season-adjusted
time of death (TOD)**. Within-tissue TMM normalization and log-CPM calculation
follow the normalization step of [Talamanca et al.
(2023)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.add0846). The builder retains samples
with valid TOD, keeps the first gene for each symbol, and selects genes with
mean log-CPM greater than 3. Cosinor models are fitted to normalized expression.
The GTEx project reference is the [GTEx Consortium atlas
(2020)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaz1776).

SCP estimates each gene's acrophase relative to the input time. Power
simulations reuse the prepared pilot.

```{r discover}
head(scp_pilots()[, c("species", "dataset", "tissue", "condition", "design")])
scp_pilot_search(species = "human", tissue_pattern = "caudate")
```

Load a bundled pilot as a ready-to-use `CircadianBioOptions` object:

```{r load-pilot}
bio <- scp_load_pilot("human", "GSE160521", "Caudate", "Control")

bio$ngenes <- 1200L

design <- CircadianDesignOptions(
  sample_sizes = c(20, 40, 60, 80, 120),
  nsims        = 20,
  design       = "passive",
  cts          = bio$cts
)

analysis <- CircadianAnalysisOptions(
  alpha           = 0.05,
  p.adjust.method = "BH",
  r_strata        = makeAdaptiveRStrata(bio, bin_width = 0.25)
)
```

SCP estimates power conditional on the fitted pilot, input time, sampling
design, and model. Users can also provide their own expression data and sample
times.
The cosinor model describes mean expression over input time and does not
require the sampling times to follow a cosine distribution.

The app uses TOD for bundled GTEx pilots and keeps uploaded collection times
unchanged.

```{r input-time-basis}
head(scp_pilots(species = "human")[,
  c("dataset", "tissue", "gtex_release", "time_basis", "n")])

# A Liver design uses its aggregate seasonal-TOD distribution.
bio_liver <- scp_load_pilot("human", "GTEx", "Liver", "All")
design_liver <- CircadianDesignOptions(
  sample_sizes = c(120, 240, 360), nsims = 20,
  design = "passive", cts = bio_liver$time_distribution
)
```

The source manifest records the v10 inputs and exclusions. Earlier package
versions remain available through the GitHub release history.

---

# Single-cohort power

`runSimsSingleCohort()` sweeps N under the pilot signal-to-noise ratio distribution and
returns a rich result that feeds `plotSingleCohortPower()`. The detector is the
cosinor F-test. `K = 1` is the single-harmonic (24 h) model.

```{r single, message = FALSE}
res <- runSimsSingleCohort(
  bio.opts      = bio,
  design.opts   = design,
  analysis.opts = analysis,
  K             = 1,
  mc.cores      = NCORES,
  verbose       = FALSE
)

data.frame(N = res$sample_sizes,
           power = round(rowMeans(res$marginal_power, na.rm = TRUE), 3),
           MCSE = round(apply(res$marginal_power, 1, sd) / sqrt(res$nsims), 3))
```

`npower()` reads the smallest N that reaches a target power at a target FDR
(interpolated between grid points). It returns `NA` if the grid never reaches
the target. Extend the grid or increase the number of experiments as needed.

```{r npower}
np <- npower(res, target_power = 0.80, fdr = 0.05)
np$n
```

```{r plot-single, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 4.2}
plotSingleCohortPower(res, title = "Caudate control, passive single-cohort power",
                      fdr = 0.05, reference_n = 60)
```

Panel A is the marginal power curve at several FDR levels. Panel B stratifies
power by the per-gene signal-to-noise ratio $r = A / \sigma$. Panel C shows the
true-discovery count per stratum.

---

# Bring your own data

In practice you start from your own pilot: a gene-by-sample expression matrix
plus a vector of collection times (hours). SCP bundles a small demo matrix in
`inst/extdata/example_caudate_liver.rds`. Its synthetic Caudate and Liver
arms each contain 1,200 genes by 48 independent simulated samples, with six
scheduled times and eight samples per time. The fixture was generated from a
joint aggregate calibration and contains no observed donor expression or
individual TOD values. Swap in your own `expr` / `times` to fit your data.

```{r own-data}
ex <- readRDS(system.file("extdata", "example_caudate_liver.rds", package = "SCP"))
expr  <- ex$caudate$expr      # genes x independent simulated samples
times <- ex$caudate$times     # scheduled simulation times in hours
dim(expr)

bio_own <- estCircadianParam(expr, times, period = 24, top_k = "all", verbose = FALSE)
cat(sprintf("Own pilot: %d genes, %.1f%% rhythmic, median r = %.2f\n",
            bio_own$ngenes, 100 * bio_own$prop_rhythmic,
            median(bio_own$amplitude / bio_own$sigma_rhythmic, na.rm = TRUE)))
```

Here `top_k = "all"` retains every rhythmic synthetic gene. `bio_own` plugs
into the same `runSimsSingleCohort()` call as a bundled pilot. Estimated phases
are already in hours.

```{r phase-hours}
summary(bio_own$phase %% bio_own$period)
```

---

# Two-harmonic detection (K = 2)

`K = 2` adds a 12 h harmonic and two fitted coefficients. The extra component
can capture waveforms that depart from a single cosine. The comparison below
keeps the first-harmonic Caudate truth and changes only the detector. It is a
sensitivity example, separate from a matched comparison with two-harmonic
truth. Identifiability needs at least `2K + 1` distinct sampling phases
(B >= 5 for K = 2).

```{r k2, message = FALSE}
res_K2 <- runSimsSingleCohort(bio.opts = bio, design.opts = design,
                              analysis.opts = analysis, K = 2,
                              mc.cores = NCORES, verbose = FALSE)

data.frame(N        = res$sample_sizes,
           power_K1 = round(rowMeans(res$marginal_power,    na.rm = TRUE), 3),
           power_K2 = round(rowMeans(res_K2$marginal_power, na.rm = TRUE), 3))
```

---

# Differential power (DR, DP, DM)

For two-group studies, estimate a two-group pilot with
`estCircadianParamTwoGroup()` and run `runDifferentialPower()`. The example below
fits the synthetic Caudate and Liver arms. The fitted parameters and results
belong to this demonstration, not the original cohorts or official figures.
Sparse fitted components can use the estimator's fallback effect ranges.

```{r diff, message = FALSE}
bio_diff <- estCircadianParamTwoGroup(
  data_1  = ex$caudate$expr, data_2  = ex$liver$expr,
  times_1 = ex$caudate$times, times_2 = ex$liver$times,
  top_k = "all",
  paired_sigma = TRUE,         # preserve each arm's selected amplitude/noise pairs
  verbose = FALSE
)

bio_diff$diagnostics[c("n_DR_genes_pilot", "n_DP_genes_pilot", "n_DM_genes_pilot")]

design_d <- CircadianDesignOptions(
  sample_sizes = c(24, 48, 72),
  nsims        = 3,
  design       = "passive",
  cts          = bio_diff$cts,
  test_types   = c("DR", "DP", "DM")
)

res_diff <- runDifferentialPower(
  bio_diff, design_d, CircadianAnalysisOptions(alpha = 0.05),
  methods    = "DCP",
  test_types = c("DR", "DP", "DM"),
  mc.cores   = NCORES,
  plot       = FALSE,
  verbose    = FALSE
)

# Recommended N per endpoint at 80% power, FDR 20%
sapply(c("DR", "DP", "DM"),
       function(ep) unname(npower(res_diff, target_power = 0.80, fdr = 0.20, endpoint = ep)$n))
```

```{r plot-diff, fig.width = 11, fig.height = 9}
plotDiffPower(list(res_diff),
              comp_labels    = "Synthetic Caudate vs Liver",
              endpoints      = c("DR", "DP", "DM"),
              fdr_thresholds = c(0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.20),
              panel_fdr      = 0.05,
              vline_fdr      = 0.20)
```

**Interpreting the endpoints.** DR (differential rhythmicity): a gene oscillates
in one condition but not the other. DP (differential phase): it oscillates in
both but the peak shifts. DM (differential mesor): it oscillates in both but the
baseline shifts (analogous to differential expression). Compare the estimated
curves to assess which endpoint needs more samples. This short run has few
target genes for some endpoints and is not a stable power estimate.

## Customizing the differential scenario

`runDifferentialPower()` uses each arm's selected amplitude/noise pairs for its
DR-only genes. Jointly rhythmic genes share noise scale and baseline expression
except for the specified DM shift, and the two arms have independent errors.
You can change the fractions and effect ranges to explore a hypothetical study.
Keep the total rhythmic proportion large enough to contain the assigned classes.

| field | controls |
|---|---|
| `prop_DR`, `prop_DP`, `prop_DM` | fraction of genes that differ in rhythmicity / phase / mesor |
| `phase_diff` + `dp_shift_mode` | DP phase shift in hours. `"fixed"` uses `phase_diff[2]`. `"uniform"` draws in the range. |
| `mesor_diff` | DM baseline-shift range |
| `dr_amp_scale` | global multiplier on rhythmic amplitude (signal-to-noise ratio sensitivity) |
| `dr_sigma_scale` | global multiplier on noise (signal-to-noise ratio sensitivity) |

```{r diff-scenario, message = FALSE}
bio_plan <- bio_diff
bio_plan$prop_rhythmic  <- 0.40        # enough rhythmic genes for these classes
bio_plan$prop_DR        <- 0.15        # hypothesize 15% differentially rhythmic
bio_plan$prop_DP        <- 0.10        # 10% phase-shifted
bio_plan$prop_DM        <- 0.05        # 5% mesor-shifted
bio_plan$phase_diff     <- c(6, 6)     # a fixed six-hour phase shift
bio_plan$dp_shift_mode  <- "fixed"     # fixed shift = phase_diff[2] (vs "uniform")
bio_plan$dr_amp_scale   <- 1.0         # signal-to-noise ratio as in pilot
bio_plan$dr_sigma_scale <- 1.0

res_plan <- runDifferentialPower(
  bio_plan,
  CircadianDesignOptions(sample_sizes = c(24, 48, 72), nsims = 3,
                         design = "passive", cts = bio_plan$cts,
                         test_types = c("DR", "DP", "DM")),
  CircadianAnalysisOptions(alpha = 0.05),
  methods = "DCP", test_types = c("DR", "DP", "DM"),
  mc.cores = NCORES, plot = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)

# power at the largest N (FDR 20%) for each endpoint under this scenario
sapply(c("DR", "DP", "DM"),
       function(ep) round(tail(npower(res_plan, 0.80, 0.20, endpoint = ep)$power, 1), 3))
```

To stress-test a weaker-than-pilot effect, lower `dr_amp_scale` (or raise
`dr_sigma_scale`) and compare the estimated curves. Use more experiments to
separate Monte Carlo variation from the effect of the changed scenario.

---

# B vs m design trade-off

At a fixed total N, how should you spread samples across time points (B) versus
replicates per time point (m = N / B)? `recommendDesign()` runs guidance plus a
simulation sweep over a B x N grid. For the single-harmonic cosinor F-test,
exactly balanced, equally spaced designs with B >= 3 have the same harmonic
information at fixed N under Gaussian first-harmonic truth. The small simulation
below illustrates separate active study planning, and Monte Carlo variation can
still separate its estimated curves.

```{r bvsm, message = FALSE}
rec <- recommendDesign(
  bio.opts      = bio,
  design.opts   = CircadianDesignOptions(sample_sizes = c(24, 48, 72),
                                         nsims = 5, design = "active",
                                         cts = seq(0, 20, by = 4),
                                         B_values = c(3, 6)),
  analysis.opts = CircadianAnalysisOptions(alpha = 0.05),
  methods        = "DCP",
  target_power   = 0.80,
  mode           = "single",
  run_simulation = TRUE,
  mc.cores       = NCORES,
  plot           = FALSE,
  verbose        = FALSE
)
rec$simulation$power_df
```

---

# Bootstrap uncertainty

When the pilot is small, the recommended N is itself uncertain.
`runBootstrapDesignGrid()` resamples the pilot's subjects with replacement
(the Efron nonparametric bootstrap, `resample = "subject"`, the default),
refits the pilot summary, and re-estimates power on each draw. This example uses
the synthetic Caudate arm. The deliberately small number of bootstrap draws
shows the API, not a reliable uncertainty interval. Increase both `nboot` and
`nsims_inner` and check stability before interpreting the intervals.

```{r bootstrap, message = FALSE}
boot_opts <- CircadianBootstrapOptions(
  design_vector = seq(0, 20, by = 4),
  B_values      = 6,
  N_values      = c(24, 48),
  nboot         = 3,
  nsims_inner   = 3,
  design        = "active",
  seed          = 42
)

boot_res <- runBootstrapDesignGrid(
  pilot_data    = ex$caudate$expr,
  pilot_times   = ex$caudate$times,
  boot.opts     = boot_opts,
  analysis.opts = CircadianAnalysisOptions(alpha = 0.05, fdr_thresholds = 0.05),
  bio_diff.opts = bio_own,    # calibrated from the same synthetic input
  mode          = "single",
  methods       = "DCP",
  mc.cores      = NCORES,
  verbose       = FALSE
)
boot_res$power_mean
```

These demonstration intervals summarize resampling of the synthetic pilot.
They are not a replacement for the official bootstrap analysis.

---

# Working with result objects

`runSimsSingleCohort()` and `runDifferentialPower()` return rich lists. Save them
with `saveRDS()` and replot at any FDR threshold later without re-simulating.

```{r result-objects, eval = FALSE}
saveRDS(res, "single_cohort_power.rds")

res$sample_sizes     # N values swept
res$marginal_power   # [N x nsims] marginal power
res$strat_power      # [N x r_strata x nsims] power stratified by signal-to-noise ratio
res$pvalues          # [N x genes x nsims] raw p-values (replot at any FDR)

res_diff$fdr_DR      # [genes x N x nsims] BH-adjusted p-values for DR
res_diff$fdr_DP      # ... BH-adjusted p-values for DP
res_diff$fdr_DM      # ... BH-adjusted p-values for DM
res_diff$diff_type   # per-gene ground-truth type per simulation
```

---

# Function reference

| Function | Purpose |
|----------|---------|
| `scp_pilots()`, `scp_pilot_search()`, `scp_load_pilot()` | Browse and load bundled pilots |
| `estCircadianParam()` | Estimate single-group pilot parameters from raw data |
| `estCircadianParamTwoGroup()` | Estimate two-group pilot parameters |
| `CircadianDesignOptions()` | Build the design option object |
| `CircadianAnalysisOptions()` | Build the analysis option object |
| `makeAdaptiveRStrata()` | Build adaptive r-strata breaks from a pilot |
| `runSimsSingleCohort()` | Single-cohort power (K = 1 or 2) |
| `runDifferentialPower()` | Differential power (DR, DP, DM) |
| `npower()` | Recommended N at a target power and FDR |
| `recommendDesign()` | B vs m design orchestrator |
| `runBootstrapDesignGrid()` | Bootstrap pilot-uncertainty quantification |
| `plotSingleCohortPower()`, `plotDiffPower()` | Power figures |
| `launchShiny()` | Launch the bundled point-and-click app |
